edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: workers chronically exposed to diesel exhaust
edges.mechanism: Diesel exhaust contains soot-bound PAHs and reactive particles that deposit deep in the lung and drive chronic oxidative DNA damage, supporting its link to lung cancer.
edges.summary: For lung cancer, the most useful starting point is the 2025 Collatuzzo meta analysis in Med Lav. It found that diesel exhaust exposure tracks with higher risk or worse outcomes, and the follow-on evidence is broadly consistent even when absolute benefit or harm is modest.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
